narration.full_text: Now, let's put prime factorization into practice by finding the Highest Common Factor, or HCF, and the Least Common Multiple, or LCM, of two numbers. We'll use the numbers 72 and 120 as our example. First, we perform the prime factorization for each number. For 72, this gives us two to the power of three times three to the power of two. For 120, we get two to the power of three times three times five. To find the HCF, we identify the common prime factors and take the lowest power of each. In this case, both numbers share two to the power of three and three to the power of one. Multiplying these together gives us an HCF of 24. For the LCM, we take all prime factors present in either number and use the highest power of each. So, we'll use two to the power of three, three to the power of two, and five to the power of one. Multiplying these highest powers results in an LCM of 360. This method ensures we capture all factors for the LCM and only common factors for the HCF.
